approach.method_basis: The Parent is a genetic algorithm that breeds molecular graphs from a population of up to sixty-four scored molecules. It draws parents from three high-ranking score bands, makes connected-fragment crossovers and local atom or bond edits, and sends each valid, novel offspring directly for evaluation. Accepted scores immediately update a greedy survivor population, so useful offspring can become parents of the next batch. This feedback loop worked, but most evaluated offspring scored below their generating parents.
approach.novelty: Add posterior-sampling selection before offspring reach the oracle. The same graph operators first generate a fresh pool; a fingerprint Gaussian process learned only from this task's accepted scores draws plausible score functions, and each batch position takes a different sampled function's best available offspring. This concentrates evaluations on promising generated structures while allowing uncertainty to change the choices. The lineage has only its root so far: no sibling has tested learned offspring selection, and the supplied mechanism-cluster history is empty. The new mechanism changes which generated offspring are evaluated; its training archive and diagnostics support that single selection mechanism.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-4fa9546e559e achieved a screening macro mean of 0.491654854899 with valid graph evolution and all registered root observables active, but only 201 of 1450 accepted offspring strictly beat their best breeding parent (0.138620689655), and mean child-minus-best-parent score was -0.0841535792773. That mean was negative on every task. The actual summary and run log report successful complete execution with no external invalid or duplicate proposals; generation validity is therefore not the observed limitation. The limiting behavior is direct oracle submission of unselected graph offspring despite a large fraction of unproductive edits. These are single-seed observations, not a paired causal estimate of a filtering benefit.
hypothesis: Select oracle-bound offspring by maximizing independent joint posterior function draws from a task-local fingerprint Gaussian process over a fresh pool generated by the Parent's unchanged graph evolution operators.

finding_summary.headline: Posterior selection reproduces across seeds, but offspring yield stays below the historical parent-beating rate
finding_summary.insights: The experiment now separates reliable selector execution from the hoped-for improvement in offspring yield. The new runs' posterior means contain useful predictive information on the selected molecules: pooled prediction MSE is 0.017182 versus 0.036613 for the same-fit archive mean, with average within-batch rank correlation 0.412. Yet this information and widespread uncertainty-driven choice do not produce a higher parent-beating fraction. The remaining question is how to turn predictive information into more productive evaluations relative to already strong parents. Prediction quality is also uneven: on sitagliptin_mpo it is worse than the archive-mean predictor in two of three seeds, and that objective has the largest final-score variation. The chemistry assessment shows ample aromatic amides, cyclic amines and carbonyl-containing rings, alongside reactive substitutions and destructive edits; access to recognizable molecular families is established, while reliable discrimination among useful, chemically credible alternatives remains open. The unused pool members have no scores, so these runs cannot identify which rejected alternatives would have been better. Matched Parent replicas and same-pool comparisons with mean-only and generation-order selection are needed to isolate score benefit, efficiency, and uncertainty's contribution.
finding_summary.results: The two additional runs reproduce posterior selection and feedback. All 2,900 selected offspring maximize their reconstructed correlated function draws, uncertainty changes 2,693 choices (92.86%) compared with choosing the highest posterior mean, and all 2,800 eligible predictions on the same molecules change after accepted feedback. All 290 fits use only earlier accepted observations. Mean final-best score across the five objectives is 0.558863 in the first additional run and 0.526723 in the second, compared with 0.547535 in the original run of this selector. Across all three seeds, mean score is 0.544374 with population standard deviation 0.013310. The intended offspring-efficiency improvement does not appear: only 371 of 2,900 new offspring beat their best generating parent (12.79%), and their mean child-minus-parent score is -0.100465. The original direct-submission Parent's single-seed references are 13.86% and -0.084154. Across all three selector runs, 565 of 4,350 offspring beat their best parent (12.99%). The original paired screening-score gain of 0.055880 remains a one-seed comparison because matched additional runs of the direct-submission Parent are unavailable.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides, cyclic amines and dicarbonyl heterocycles are abundant, but reactive halogen and peroxide substitutions persist.
molecular.overall_character: Every task has 600 observed molecules across seeds 1 and 2, including 580 optimizer proposals. Ring_closure_rate ranges from 0.9724 to 0.9966 and aromatic_atom_rate from 0.969 to 0.9897, supporting a predominantly ring-rich aromatic repertoire. These counters measure SMILES-text presence, not ring counts or fractions of aromatic atoms. The molecules include benzofused nitrogen heterocycles with aryl amides, bridged lactams, carbonyl-rich fused heteroaromatics, saturated cyclic aminals, macrocyclic nitrogen/carbonyl systems and fluorinated aryl primary amines. Thus useful rings, amines, carbonyls and heteroaromatic chemistry are demonstrably available. Mean SMILES lengths range from 45.0 to 85.3 and the maximum reaches 248; moderately sized leaders coexist with bulky assembled structures and occasional tiny fragments. Charged_rate is 0.0 throughout, which does not mean that neutral SMILES lack protonatable amines. Stereocentre_rate is also 0.0 despite several asymmetric saturated centres, ring junctions and constrained frameworks. The main chemical-quality issue is the persistence of nitrogen-halogen, oxygen-halogen and peroxide functionality, including among high-scoring structures. Some leading molecules are much more conventional, especially the primary-amine-bearing fluorinated aryl dicarbonyl family and ordinary carbon-linked cyclic amines. Synthetic plausibility is therefore mixed, and drug-likeness moderate overall. Core diversity is greater across runs than within their concentrated upper families; numerous local ring and substituent variants should not be mistaken for uniformly broad useful chemistry. The supplied parent_trajectories are seed 0 of n-fc2c108a5253 itself. Comparisons below describe those different runs and do not judge algorithm activation. Missing chemistry denotes gaps in the observed output, not established benefits for unobserved replacements.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 2 favours moderately sized benzofused unsaturated nitrogen-nitrogen rings bearing a carboxanilide, methoxy and methyl groups. The leading carboxanilide nitrogen is fluorinated, and other variants halogenate the ring nitrogen or add bromomethyl/chloromethyl groups. Seed 1 instead produces bridged or spiro-like lactam/imine frameworks containing an aromatic nitrogen ring and vinyl ether or vinyl sulfide decoration; some introduce sulfur-nitrogen bridges. Ring_closure_rate is 0.9724, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9707 and halogen_rate 0.8224. Recognizable amide and heterocycle chemistry is retained, but neither the N-fluoro amides nor all of the bridged sulfur variants are routine medicinal substitutions. Prior seed 0 reached 0.4463521672202675 with a bridged aromatic nitrogen/oxygen system bearing an aryl-containing ketone side chain. The new high families change core chemistry but remain below that observed best.
liabilities: N-fluoro amides, N-halogenated hydrazine-like rings and halomethyl substituents introduce reactive functionality into the high tail.
Nitrogen-nitrogen, sulfur-nitrogen and oxime-ether-like linkages add stability or configurational questions to already constrained structures.
Tiny late fragments discard the useful molecule rather than providing a coherent small analogue; bridged stereochemistry remains unspecified.
missing_features: Stable local alternatives to N-fluoro amides, ring-nitrogen halogenation and sulfur-nitrogen bridges are incompletely represented in the leading series, although a more conventional bridged lactam already reaches the upper neighbourhood.
Broader independent cores preserving the useful aromatic and carbonyl relationships are not established beyond the concentrated fused-nitrogen and bridged-lactam families.
Explicit configuration at asymmetric bridged centres and credible core-preserving contractions are absent from parts of the output.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxyindole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. The N-fluoro carboxanilide on the benzofused hydrazine-like ring reaches 0.4163503402962837, while the vinyl-sulfide, sulfur-nitrogen-bridged lactam/imine reaches 0.4126819838532174. A related vinyl-ether bridged lactam without that sulfur bridge scores 0.4005670758913022, showing a relatively conventional alternative in the same broad upper range. Adding chlorine or fluorine to the hydrazine-ring nitrogen gives 0.40314990987966176; changing the ring nitrogen pair to an oxygen/nitrogen connection gives 0.36286362320121707. A related imidamide-containing fused ring scores 0.40497388700123543. These observations favour coherent aromatic/polar cyclic arrangements over indiscriminate halogen addition. Ethene, methane, molecular fluorine and small sulfur or imine fragments appear at 0.0, and the seed-2 trajectory ends with ethene at 0.0. The useful cores are therefore not consistently preserved in all emissions.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-1 molecules join carbonyl-containing oxygen/nitrogen heteroaromatic ring systems through an amino linkage. They are heavily decorated with halogens, short ring bridges and, often, oxygen-oxygen-halogen chains. Several also carry an O-cyanate substituent, which is chemically different from a carbon-bound nitrile. Seed 2 develops a related but distinct family of coupled and bridged nitrogen dicarbonyl heterocycles with N-halogenation and halomethyl substitution. Ring_closure_rate and aromatic_atom_rate are both 0.9862; halogen_rate is 0.9552. Mean_smiles_length 85.3 and max_smiles_length 248 show a substantial bulky-assembly tail, although the supplied leaders are more compact than the most extended proposals. The prior seed-0 best, 0.6004556752278376, was a much more extensively assembled nitrogen/carbonyl heteroaromatic structure with conjugated appendages. The new upper structures are more compact connected heterocycles but introduce pronounced reactive-group liabilities.
liabilities: Oxygen-oxygen-halogen chains, oxygen-halogen bonds and O-cyanate groups make the leading chemistry substantially more reactive than an ordinary halogenated heteroaryl series.
Seed-2 late structures repeatedly carry nitrogen-fluorine or nitrogen-chlorine bonds, adding a separate stability concern.
Short bridges across aromatic frameworks and very large connected assemblies create geometric and synthetic demands that the score alone does not resolve.
missing_features: Chemically robust substituents that preserve the useful heteroaromatic arrangement are underrepresented relative to peroxide and heteroatom-halogen variants. The fluoromethyl analogue demonstrates that a less reactive alternative can retain a similar score.
Independent stable scaffold and linker alternatives are incompletely represented within the leading coupled-heterocycle families.
Reliable control of short ring bridges and avoidance of unnecessary multi-core concatenation are missing from parts of the broader output.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading amino-linked heterocycle with an oxygen-oxygen-chlorine substituent scores 0.6324703199409752. A closely related aza-ring version scores 0.6300605077662029, whereas replacing its oxygen-oxygen-chlorine group with fluoromethyl gives 0.6293992623616929. Chlorinated and brominated oxygen-containing side-chain alternatives also score 0.6293992623616929. Thus a nearly comparable upper value is observed with an ordinary carbon-bound fluorine substituent; the peroxide/oxygen-halogen motif is not demonstrably essential. A less bridged analogue scores 0.6309644029285534. The initial dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.548381482770623, and tiny chlorine, fluoromethane, enol-ether or cyanogen-halide fragments occupy the 0.5 floor. Late seed-2 nitrogen-halogen-rich dicarbonyl assemblies remain around 0.6058710298363812 and 0.6012872454997692. The gradient supports a specific connected heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangement over isolated fragments or arbitrary size, while being relatively insensitive to some chemically consequential peripheral substitutions.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-2 molecules combine halogenated aromatic rings with a saturated imidazolidine-type aminal ring, secondary or tertiary amines, and short aminoalkyl or enamine-containing connections to another substituted aromatic group. The leading central aminal carbon also bears an amino substituent. These are moderately large, recognizable amine-rich medicinal architectures, although aminal stability and some reactive substitutions remain concerns. Seed 1 reaches a different, more bridged amine/aryl family. Ring_closure_rate is 0.9828, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9724, halogen_rate 0.9828 and mean_smiles_length 58.7. Formal charge markers are absent, but accessible basic centres are abundant in the leading SMILES. The prior seed-0 leader scored 0.9908331648929692 and used a more rigid spiro saturated-amine framework between halogenated and thiol-substituted aromatic groups. Both old and new upper families clearly contain cyclic amines and substantial aromatic surface.
liabilities: Amino-substituted aminal centres, enamine functionality and multiple basic nitrogens require stability and physicochemical scrutiny beyond their high scores.
Chloromethyl, bromomethyl and thiol-containing side chains occur among near-leading variants.
The structures combine substantial aromatic/halogen content with basic centres, and some late variants disturb the aromatic or amine environment instead of preserving a coherent analogue.
missing_features: No absence of basic cyclic amines is supported; the missing coverage is stable, well-defined alternatives to the aminoaminal/enamine architecture that preserve its useful amine and aromatic relationships.
Control of nitrogen acylation, aromaticity and linker attachment is inconsistent, with some local changes losing much of the observed score.
Defined stereochemistry at the substituted aminoalkyl and aminal centres is missing; the trajectory does not establish a preferred configuration.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The amino-substituted imidazolidine with a carbon-linked secondary amine reaches 0.9914038363125457. The otherwise related example without that central amino substituent scores 0.9725868595115974. The enamine-connected counterpart scores 0.981088217863691, and its N-formyl analogue scores 0.48797702544581545, supporting a role for the local electronic state of the ring nitrogen. A halomethyl-substituted relative remains high at 0.989167131859766, whereas dearomatizing its terminal halogenated ring in a related family gives 0.08210159005746291. Removing the second aryl-containing amine side chain and retaining a hydroxylamine-like fragment yields 0.011495655106721757. Simple halogenated benzenes score 0.001421581552029289 and 0.0021330149885975206, while the acylated amino-acid starting-family derivative scores 0.000719339566735797. The visible preference is for the connected amine/aryl arrangement, not aromatic surface, amine count or halogenation alone.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 1 favours aryl-substituted bridged or fused nitrogen rings carrying multiple carbonyls, with an ethoxy benzofuran-like region and an N-fluoro centre in its leading structures. Seed 2 instead develops quinoline-linked macrocyclic nitrogen/carbonyl systems containing tertiary amines, amide-like carbonyls, and hydroxyl, methyl or thiol substitutions. These molecules range from medium-sized macrocycles to bulkier fused systems and have recognizable synthetic building blocks, although their full ring topology and some substitutions are demanding. Ring_closure_rate is 0.9966, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9897 and mean_smiles_length 56.6. The prior seed-0 best, 0.22405709718343647, was another nitrogen/carbonyl ring system combining aromatic and saturated regions. The new leaders change ring layout but remain in a similar chemical class and below that score.
liabilities: The leading seed-1 structures contain nitrogen-fluorine bonds, whereas a near-leading seed-2 macrocycle demonstrates a conventional alternative without that functionality.
Multiple carbonyls, tertiary amines and constrained ring systems create conformational and synthetic complexity; thiol-containing analogues add oxidation concerns.
Small cyclic peroxide fragments and overgrown multi-aryl variants occur at lower scores, showing that ring presence alone is not sufficient chemical organization.
missing_features: A broader set of stable cores that retain the useful macrocyclic or bridged nitrogen/carbonyl arrangement is not established beyond closely related upper families.
Coherent simplification and linker changes are incompletely explored: useful medium-sized macrocycles exist, but both fragmentation and further core duplication can lose the favourable arrangement.
Defined configuration at bridged saturated centres and adequate specification of constrained-ring geometry are missing.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial diaryl dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.1678386594791329. The N-fluoro bridged carbonyl structure reaches 0.2133697489012744, while the more conventionally bonded hydroxyquinoline-linked macrocycle scores 0.21037674112349405 and a related azaaryl/carbonyl macrocycle scores 0.20917089553667287. Hydroxyl-, methyl- and thiol-containing relatives share 0.20736246951923798, so those particular peripheral changes do not distinguish their recorded scores. Phenol alone scores 0.06793662204867576, the small aryl amide acid scores 0.07504633196017493, and ethane and a small cyclic peroxide score 0.012461119656980673 and 0.0239774717598468. A late structure adding a second quinoline-containing region scores only 0.1754730092490373. The apparent preference is for organized aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl relationships and suitable ring size, not maximal molecular growth or N-fluorination as a universal requirement.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-1 family is a moderately sized, fluorinated aryl primary-amine series attached to a bicyclic nitrogen dicarbonyl heterocycle. The best molecule carries aminomethyl, aryl fluorine and fluoromethyl groups with ordinary carbon-bound fluorination; its core nitrogens are alkylated rather than directly fluorinated. Other high relatives use aminoethyl groups, fused small carbocycles or N-fluorination. This leading chemistry is more recognizable and plausibly makeable than the much larger linked dicarbonyl assemblies in the low tail. Seed 2 reaches a different fused heteroaromatic family with small fluorinated carbocycles, hydroxyl and thiomethyl groups. Ring_closure_rate is 0.9724, aromatic_atom_rate 0.969, halogen_rate 0.781 and mean_smiles_length 56.5. The prior seed-0 best, 0.4759777345546235, used an acylated nitrogen-rich fluorinated heterocycle with an unsaturated oxygen ring. The new highest family brings a clear primary-amine/aryl/dicarbonyl arrangement into the upper output.
liabilities: Direct nitrogen-fluorine bonds occur in several high relatives even though the leading molecule demonstrates ordinary carbon-bound fluorination and N-alkylation.
Other variants contain strained small unsaturated carbocycles, thiols or thiomethyl groups; their stability and stereochemical accessibility are not established.

Large duplicated or fused dicarbonyl assemblies produce substantial bulk with extremely poor recorded scores, indicating a need for coherent size and core organization rather than further concatenation.
missing_features: The useful primary amine is present in the leading family, but stable alternative cores and linkers preserving its placement relative to the aryl dicarbonyl system remain incompletely represented.
Consistent retention of the favourable local amino group is missing in some substitutions and in the alternative fused heteroaromatic trajectory.
Stereochemically specified small-ring variants are absent where configuration becomes relevant; the leading acyclic side-chain example itself does not require an assigned tetrahedral stereocentre.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aminomethyl, fluoromethyl-substituted aryl dicarbonyl leader scores 0.5845583988949146. Replacing a peripheral fluoromethyl group with chlorine in the otherwise corresponding structure gives 0.5064928497454653. An aminoethyl analogue scores 0.5180292619150341; the full trajectory shows its closely matched terminal-amine-to-fluorine replacement at 0.0007365197806377691, supporting the importance of that local primary-amine functionality in this family. N-fluorinated aminoethyl relatives score 0.5652209810580261 and 0.5615749101173619, below the conventionally N-alkylated leader. Very large linked dicarbonyl molecules score 1.6758614448245604e-53 and 5.4391203474237023e-42. Seed 2 reaches 0.4071395189354175 with a small fluorinated carbocycle attached to its fused aromatic core, but ends at 0.0038179150668162477 after losing that substituent and changing nearby sulfur decoration. The gradient supports compact, correctly placed amine/aryl/carbonyl relationships; neither total fluorination nor accumulating more copies of the core is a sufficient rule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited upper families contain N-fluoro amides and amines, oxygen-oxygen-halogen chains, oxygen-halogen bonds and O-cyanate substituents. Yet a fluoromethyl alternative scores 0.6293992623616929 near its peroxide-bearing relative at 0.6300605077662029, a conventional macrocycle scores 0.21037674112349405 near an N-fluorinated leader, and an ordinarily N-alkylated aryl primary amine leads another family at 0.5845583988949146. The data show usable conventional chemistry alongside reactive edits.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently prefer chemically robust local alternatives over reactive heteroatom-halogen and peroxide substitutions.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make stable functional-group replacements available while preserving the useful core and polar-group relationships. Treat carbon-bound halogens, nitrogen-halogen bonds and oxygen/peroxide-halogen chains as distinct chemistry, and use accepted molecular feedback to compare coherent alternatives instead of treating all halogen substitutions alike.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A connected cyclic-aminal/amine structure scores 0.9914038363125457, whereas deleting its second aryl-containing amine region gives 0.011495655106721757. In a related family, nitrogen formylation changes a 0.981088217863691 structure to one scoring 0.48797702544581545. The fluorinated aryl primary-amine family also shows a sharp loss when an aminoethyl terminus is replaced by fluorine. These observations establish local arrangement, not merely nitrogen or halogen abundance, as useful visible chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful amine and carbonyl attachment context is not reliably preserved during local substitution, acylation or linker changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve and deliberately vary the spacing, attachment and electronic environment of amines, aromatic groups and carbonyls. Distinguish free or cyclic amines from acylated, oxygen-linked or sulfur-linked nitrogen so feedback can assess chemically meaningful local changes.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Tiny ethene, methane and halogen fragments occupy zero or floor-score tails, while large duplicated dicarbonyl assemblies score 1.6758614448245604e-53 and 5.4391203474237023e-42. A late macrocycle acquiring an additional quinoline region scores 0.1754730092490373, below simpler relatives near 0.21037674112349405. Conversely, some useful molecules are themselves moderately large and cyclic, so the evidence does not support a universal size minimum or maximum.
transferable_gaps.gap: Size changes can discard useful cores or duplicate them into bulky assemblies instead of producing coherent analogues.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide core-preserving growth, contraction and linker moves that maintain complete functional groups. Let accepted observations determine useful size locally while maintaining alternatives to both fragmentation and repeated assembly of the same core.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. The cited molecules include asymmetric aminoalkyl centres, substituted aminal carbons, bridged lactams and fluorinated small carbocycles. Such structures can have configurational alternatives even though all supplied strings omit stereocentre annotations. Short bridges and constrained rings also need more than a valid ring-closure string to define plausible geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Explicit stereochemistry and controlled geometric interpretation are missing from asymmetric cyclic and bridged structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent relevant stereochemical and geometric alternatives when changing saturated centres, constrained alkenes or ring junctions. Preserve chemically credible connectivity and let accepted feedback determine useful configurations; their present absence does not establish a score benefit for any one choice.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The high tails repeatedly revisit benzofused aryl amides or bridged lactams, coupled carbonyl heteroaromatics, imidazolidine-type amine architectures, quinoline-linked macrocycles and aryl primary-amine dicarbonyl systems. Different seeds reach distinct cores, so scaffold change is possible, but many leading examples differ only by local halogen, heteroatom or ring edits and some receive identical scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: Coverage of independent useful chemical cores remains narrower than the number of local analogues and peripheral edits suggests.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain several chemically distinct accepted core families and support scaffold replacements that preserve useful donor, acceptor, amine and aromatic relationships. Evaluate coverage through credible core chemistry and attachment geometry alongside molecular identity, rather than relying on a new substituent or ring closure alone.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
